text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 1951234567 - Canary rollout exhibiting elevated 5xx and high latency for requests routed to canary variant. Automatic fallback to sticky-variant policy detected. Paging oncall.

oncall-lee: got the page, I'm on it. which customers affected? how bad is the spike? assign me if needed.

sre-maya: looking now. I'm seeing a surge in 502/504 from nodes running model variant `gpt-large-alpha-canary` starting ~1951234500. Error rate ~8% on canary traffic, latency p50 -> 450ms, p95 -> 2.1s.

platform-igor: thanks Maya. Can you pull the routing logs? I want to confirm fallback pattern. We had sticky fallback enabled for this rollout.

sre-maya: pasting relevant routing trace (trimmed):
```
[1951234512] req-id=abc123 route=canary -> model=gpt-large-alpha-canary status=500
[1951234513] req-id=abc123 fallback=sticky -> model=gpt-large-stable status=200
[1951234520] req-id=def456 route=canary -> model=gpt-large-alpha-canary status=502
[1951234521] req-id=def456 fallback=sticky -> model=gpt-large-alpha-canary status=502  <-- sticky pinned wrong variant
```
Looks like fallback sticky cookie was set to canary variant in some cases, causing a ping-pong / loop.

oncall-lee: ugh. So sticky fallback is persisting the failing variant? That explains oscillation. Any recent config changes? rollout policies? Rosa you rolled this canary earlier, right?

pm-rosa: I kicked off a staged canary at 1951234400, target 5% traffic. Config used `policy: rollout-v2` with `fallback: sticky-prefer-same-variant` (that's the change from last time).

platform-igor: that fallback policy is new and apparently buggy in combination with the canary health check. Immediate mitigation options:
- pause the canary (stop routing new traffic to canary) OR
- disable sticky fallback globally OR
- force clear sticky cookies for affected customers and reroute to stable.

support-tom: customer monitoring shows elevated error rate for 3 customers on Dedicated plans, and a handful of hosted API keys with >10% failures in last 5m. Creating SEV ticket and notifying account owners.

oncall-lee: priority one: stop further user impact. I'm going to pause the canary rollout and enable immediate fallback to stable (non-sticky). On it.

sre-maya: steps to pause canary:
1) `redwood rollout pause --id rollout-v2 --env staging`
2) update routing policy: `redwood routing update --policy fallback=stable-prefer`
3) clear sticky tokens: `redis-cli KEYS "sticky:*:canary" | xargs -n1 del`

oncall-lee: executing step 1 now.

oncall-lee: (runs) `> redwood rollout pause --id rollout-v2 --env staging` -> accepted, canary traffic should stop being assigned to new sessions.

sre-maya: I'm updating routing policy to force non-sticky fallback.

platform-igor: hold on on the global clear; we should scope to sessions created after 1951234400 to avoid inadvertent state loss. Maya, can you run a targeted deletion? e.g. keys with timestamp suffix.

sre-maya: running targeted flush for keys with last-set >=1951234400. command:
```
redis-cli --scan --pattern "sticky:*" | while read k; do ts=$(redis.hget $k last_set); if [ $ts -ge 1951234400 ]; then redis.del $k; fi; done
```

sre-maya: done. Routing logs show new requests now map to stable variant.

support-tom: support: errors for affected customers dropping from 10% -> 0.8% in the last 2 min. Pinged account teams and posted incident update to status page.

pm-rosa: thanks. Quick question: why did the sticky fallback pin the canary variant? That seems like a logic bug in the policy implementation.

platform-igor: initial hypothesis: fallback path on error set sticky cookie before verifying target health. So the cookie pointed to the pre-fallback variant on subsequent retries. Repro steps incoming.

oncall-lee: for now can we keep rollout paused and mark this rollout as failed? We should also disable `sticky-prefer-same-variant` as a policy until fixed.

platform-igor: agree. I've marked rollout-v2 as halted and set global default fallback to `stable-prefer`.

sre-maya: creating a small postmortem stub: root cause = routing policy bug (sticky fallback set incorrectly), contributing = new policy not covered by e2e tests for fallback loops. Impact = transient elevated errors and latency for ~6 mins, 3 Dedicated customer incidents, brief increase in hosted API errors.

pm-rosa: assigning follow-ups: Igor to revert policy code and add unit/e2e tests (owner: platform-igor), Maya to write a remediation runbook entry for sticky fallbacks (owner: sre-maya), Support/Tom to follow up with customer comms and RCA (owner: support-tom). I'll own a full postmortem and timeline.

support-tom: filing SEV ticket and will escalate to account teams, adding notes about mitigation steps taken.

oncall-lee: thank you everyone. I'll keep the thread open for 30 minutes to monitor and then hand off to SRE rotation for cleanup. If anyone sees regression, ping here.

incident-bot: NOTE: Pager duty incident #INC-8762 created and linked to this thread.

pm-rosa: scheduling postmortem review for tomorrow at 1400 PT. Agenda: root cause, test gaps, rollout policy guardrails, and customer comms template.

platform-igor: quick patch: disabling `sticky-prefer-same-variant` flags in canary rollouts until we validate fixes in staging. Will open PR referencing this incident.

sre-maya: monitoring metrics. All green for 10m. Closing oncall shift handoff in 20.

oncall-lee: handing off to SRE rotation (sre-oncall-weekend). Leaving notes in the oncall doc.

support-tom: posting incident summary to #customer-status and emailing affected accounts.

pm-rosa: thanks team. Follow-ups tracked in the incident tracker. I'll update once postmortem is complete.

sre-maya: adding links to logs and runbook in the incident ticket: https://internal.redwood/logs/1951234567 and https://internal.redwood/runbooks/sticky-fallback

oncall-lee: thread locked to updates-only, will reopen if new alerts fire.
